<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917334_theRebbe_880" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917334_theRebbe_880__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Moshe is called the faithful shepherd, with two meanings: he nourishes Israel with faith, bringing it from an encompassing state to inwardness, and this extends to his manifestations in every generation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And to explain this,</t>
    <t s="2">the maamar first states</t>
    <t s="3">that Moshe Rabbeinu is called "Raaya Meheimna,"</t>
    <t s="4">and there are two explanations of this.</t>
    <t s="5">That he is a faithful shepherd of Israel, and that he nourishes and sustains Israel in the matter of faith.</t>
    <t s="6">For the faith that exists in Israel from their own essence—</t>
    <t s="7">that Israel are believers, children of believers—</t>
    <t s="8">can be in the category of encompassing (makif),</t>
    <t s="9">and this that Moshe shepherds and nourishes Israel in the matter of faith means that the faith should be in inwardness (penimiyus).</t>
    <t s="10">And this is what is said in the Zohar,</t>
    <t s="11">"That supernal faith will be nourished and sustained from him through you"</t>
    <t s="12">(through Moshe),</t>
    <t s="13">for this that Moshe nourishes and sustains the faith is that he draws it into inwardness.</t>
    <t s="14">And the maamar continues,</t>
    <t s="15">that this that Moshe is "Raaya Meheimna"</t>
    <t s="16">also refers to the extension of Moshe in every generation,</t>
    <t s="17">for the heads of the thousands of Israel in every generation strengthen the faith of Israel</t>
    <t s="18">(of their generation),</t>
    <t s="19">so that their faith should be in inwardness.</t>
    <t s="20">And like Mordechai,</t>
    <t s="21">who was the extension of Moshe in his generation,</t>
    <t s="22">as our sages said,</t>
    <t s="23">"Mordechai in his generation is like Moshe in his generation,"</t>
    <t s="24">for even at the time of Haman's decree,</t>
    <t s="25">when Torah study and observance of mitzvos were connected with self-sacrifice (mesirus nefesh),</t>
    <t s="26">he assembled many congregations to strengthen their faith in Hashem and to stand firm in Torah study and observance of mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="27">And after explaining at length that Moshe and his extension in every generation strengthen the faith of Israel,</t>
    <t s="28">the maamar explains</t>
    <t s="29">the precise wording of the verse, "pure olive oil, beaten for the light"</t>
    <t s="30">("for the light" [lamaor] and not "to illuminate" [leha'ir]),</t>
    <t s="31">that during the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="32">when each person is broken and crushed,</t>
    <t s="33">"beaten" (kasis),</t>
    <t s="34">through this one reaches the "light" (maor)</t>
    <t s="35">(the essence [Atzmus])</t>
    <t s="36">from which the light emanates.</t>
    <t s="37">And one must understand the connection between this explanation of "beaten for the light" and what was explained</t>
    <t s="38">(in the maamar)</t>
    <t s="39">previously, that Moshe</t>
    <t s="40">[and his extension in every generation]</t>
    <t s="41">nourishes and sustains the faith so that it should be in inwardness.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Jews in the time of Achashverosh fulfilled and received what they had begun at Mount Sinai, achieving a higher level through actual self-sacrifice, led by Mordechai.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the explanation of the verse "And you shall command" comes</t>
    <t s="2">(in the maamar)</t>
    <t s="3">as a continuation of what was explained at the beginning of the maamar,</t>
    <t s="4">that the explanation of "And the Jews received what they had begun to do"</t>
    <t s="5">is that they received what they had begun at the time of the Giving of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="6">For at the Giving of the Torah there was the beginning</t>
    <t s="7">("they began to do"),</t>
    <t s="8">and in the days of Achashverosh</t>
    <t s="9">(at the time of Haman's decree)</t>
    <t s="10">there was the receiving,</t>
    <t s="11">"and the Jews received."</t>
    <t s="12">[And as our sages said</t>
    <t s="13">on the verse,</t>
    <t s="14">"They fulfilled and received the Jews,"</t>
    <t s="15">they fulfilled what they had already received,</t>
    <t s="16">for this that they prioritized "we will do" over "we will hear" at the Giving of the Torah was only the receiving,</t>
    <t s="17">and in the days of Achashverosh</t>
    <t s="18">they fulfilled what they had received.]</t>
    <t s="19">And the maamar notes,</t>
    <t s="20">that this is seemingly astonishing,</t>
    <t s="21">for at the Giving of the Torah Israel were at the peak of elevation,</t>
    <t s="22">and there was then a revelation of G-dliness at the most sublime level</t>
    <t s="23">[in addition to the fact that even before the Giving of the Torah there were most sublime revelations,</t>
    <t s="24">the revelation at the Exodus from Egypt and especially at the Splitting of the Sea,</t>
    <t s="25">the revelation at the time of the Giving of the Torah was an even more sublime revelation],</t>
    <t s="26">and in the days of Achashverosh Israel were at the peak of descent,</t>
    <t s="27">for in addition to the concealment and hiding that is in every exile</t>
    <t s="28">[for every exile is analogous to the exile of Egypt,</t>
    <t s="29">and as it is written regarding the exile of Egypt,</t>
    <t s="30">"And they did not listen to Moshe because of shortness of spirit and hard labor,"</t>
    <t s="31">so too is it in every exile,</t>
    <t s="32">that there are many trials in the observance of Torah and mitzvos],</t>
    <t s="33">then</t>
    <t s="34">(at the time of Haman's decree)</t>
    <t s="35">the concealment and hiding was even greater,</t>
    <t s="36">and nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="37">at the time of the Giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="38">when Israel were at the peak of elevation,</t>
    <t s="39">there was only the beginning</t>
    <t s="40">("they began to do"),</t>
    <t s="41">and at the time of Haman's decree,</t>
    <t s="42">when they were at the peak of lowliness,</t>
    <t s="43">specifically then they received what they had begun at the Giving of the Torah.</t>
    <t s="44">And he explains this,</t>
    <t s="45">that at the time of the decree,</t>
    <t s="46">their observance of Torah and mitzvos was with self-sacrifice (mesirus nefesh).</t>
    <t s="47">[In addition to the fact that they had self-sacrifice not to deny G-d, heaven forbid,</t>
    <t s="48">[as explained in Torah Ohr,</t>
    <t s="49">that if they had converted they would not have been harmed,</t>
    <t s="50">for the decree was only against the Jews,</t>
    <t s="51">and nevertheless no foreign thought entered their minds, heaven forbid],</t>
    <t s="52">they had self-sacrifice also for the observance of Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="53">to the extent that they assembled many congregations to study Torah with self-sacrifice.]</t>
    <t s="54">And the arousal of their self-sacrifice was through Mordechai the Jew,</t>
    <t s="55">the Moshe of his generation.</t>
    <t s="56">And this is "And the Jews received what they had begun to do,"</t>
    <t s="57">for at the Giving of the Torah there was only the beginning, and at the time of Haman's decree there was the receiving,</t>
    <t s="58">for through their having actual self-sacrifice for Torah and mitzvos at that time, they were elevated</t>
    <t s="59">(in this matter)</t>
    <t s="60">to a more sublime level than they were at the time of the Giving of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="61">and therefore specifically then there was the receiving,</t>
    <t s="62">"and the Jews received."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The explanation of "beaten for the light" could relate to reaching self-sacrifice through being crushed, but the context suggests it also connects to Moshe nourishing faith into inwardness.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And seemingly, one could say,</t>
    <t s="1">that the explanation of "beaten for the light,"</t>
    <t s="2">that through "beaten"</t>
    <t s="3">(broken and crushed)</t>
    <t s="4">one reaches the "light" (maor),</t>
    <t s="5">is an explanation of this, that specifically at the time of the decree they came to self-sacrifice in a most sublime manner.</t>
    <t s="6">For self-sacrifice is from the essence of the soul, which is beyond revelation,</t>
    <t s="7">the "light" (maor)</t>
    <t s="8">(from which the light emanates),</t>
    <t s="9">and through being in a state of "beaten"</t>
    <t s="10">(broken and crushed),</t>
    <t s="11">the essence of the soul was revealed,</t>
    <t s="12">the "light" (maor).</t>
    <t s="13">But from the flow and order of topics in the maamar, that the explanation of "beaten for the light" comes after the topic of "Raaya Meheimna,"</t>
    <t s="14">it implies</t>
    <t s="15">that the matter of "beaten for the light" also relates to this, that Moshe nourishes and sustains the faith so that it should be in inwardness.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
